newsitem.title: USA: Perelman pushes Marvel reorganization - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Perelman pushes Marvel reorganization - WSJ.

text.p: Investor Ronald Perelman's representatives warned Marvel Entertainment Group Inc bondholders that Marvel would be forced to file for protection in bankruptcy court unless they approved a reorganization plan to massively dilute stockholders ownership position, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

The newspaper cited an analyst who attended a private meeting between the two groups as saying the representatives presented documents showing that Marvel's four main operating businesses would together report $100 million less in revenue in 1996 than in 1995.
It said the documents also showed that three of the businesses would report operating losses.

The newspaper said Marvel would also apparently need a waiver from banks to tap its credit line for $15 million and is discussing with the banks borrowing an additional $100 million to meet next year's needs.
It said a spokesman for Perelman confirmed the analyst's account of the meeting.
The Marvel Fleer/SkyBox sports and entertainment trading card unit is expected to report 1996 revenues of $203 million and post operating losses of $11 million, it said.

Marvel's new interactive unit will post a loss of $2 million, it said. The company's only healthy operating unit, the Italian sticker-and-adhesive company, Panini, will report operating earnings of $24 million and revenue is expected to be $267 million.
Perelman's Andrews Group controls Marvel and ownes 80 percent of its stock.
The story cited an analyst who attended the meeting.
